reader_notes: Read from the note text, bars 0-59 (pickup 0:3), with dump.ts for the whole piece and a throwaway comparison script to confirm the returns (bars 43-54 against 1-12, bars 35-38 against 9-12); every call was then checked by reading the passage. No published analysis was consulted. Beats are eighths. x = D E | F# E G F# E D | A G F# E F# D (0:3-2:3.5). y = the leader's rising eighths against x in the bass, A B C# D | C# B A C# D (3:1-4:3.5). w = the right hand's figuration over the dominant pedal, E C# F# D C# B | E C# D B A G# (5-6, repeated 7-8). z = a variant head of x used in the middle: an eighth, a leap up a fourth, a run of five rising sixteenths, x's first-bar figure (e.g. C# B D C# B A), then an octave drop in eighths (bass 12:1.5-14:2, right hand 13:2-16:2).

layout.form: rounded bipartite (unsure): first part 0-38 ending PAC in A, second part 38-59 returning to the whole of the opening (alpha + beta) in the tonic. Alternatives: tripartite 0-24 / 24-38 / 38-59, or four sections each closed by beta (12, 24, 38, 54).

confidence: sure for the paradigms, cadences and returns; unsure for the form label and for the primary kind
notes: The piece is laid out by its closing formula beta, which ends each section (A, b, A, then D deceptive): a ritornello-like plan more than a development of invertible lines. The middle (12-32) is two imitative sequences of x's head (z), the first rising by fifths with an octave drop after each entry, the second falling by fifths with a held note: they look like a pair, but their counterpoint differs, so I have not made them members of one paradigm. The x motive is two bars plus pickup, longer than the protocol's 'half a bar or less' for motivic-sequential; in 3/8 this is still a short motive, and nothing else fits better (the opening imitation is two bars only, not canonic; y is never exchanged). Bar 42:1 is an arrival on V of D (bass A3 A2, right hand E5) before the tonic return, a half close in effect but reached from a tonic-prolonging bass figure; not listed as a cadence.
